about: Seeded continuity cases (#78). Each answer comes from the geometry, not from a run: a box meets at 90 degrees, a fillet is tangent to a flat with a curvature step of 1/r, faces cut from one smooth surface are curvature-continuous across the cut. scripts/continuity-corpus.test.ts runs every case through the job runner and requires the exact class counts; an edge counted in a higher class than expected is a false pass and stops the line.

cases.why: Six flat faces meet at 90 degrees along 12 edges.
Every edge rounded: each fillet is tangent to its flats and its corner patches, with a curvature step of 1/3 /mm at each joint, never G2.
Each round end is two quarter cylinders of one circle (2 G2 joints); the flat sides are tangent to them with a step of 1/4 /mm (4 G1); top and bottom meet the sides at 90 degrees (12 G0).
Two half cylinders united: the side and both caps stay split along the cut, each cut edge joining pieces of one surface (4 G2); the caps meet the side halves at 90 degrees (4 G0).
A half torus and its mirror across Y0, the way a vehicle body is built from one side: every joint, the Y0 seams included, joins pieces of one torus.

cases.script: const grid = (h) => [0, 1, 2].map((i) => [0, 1, 2].map((j) => [i * 50, j * 50, i === 1 && j === 1 ? h : 0])); return sew(surface(grid(20)), surface(grid(0)));
cases.why: A domed surface sewn to a flat one along their shared boundary: they meet at an angle all round (4 G0).

cases.script: const a = Math.tan(Math.PI / 180) * 10; return polygon([[0, 0], [20, 0], [20, 2 + a], [10, 2], [0, 2]]).extrude(10);
cases.why: A plate whose top bends by 1 degree: that crease is G0 at 1 degree, ten times the G1 tolerance.
The tube's side is two faces of one swept surface (2 G2: this case found the boundary bug fixed in #86); the end caps meet it at 90 degrees (4 G0).
